scenes.text: The moth in the machine: a true story from 1947.
September 9, 1947. Harvard's Mark II computer keeps making errors.
Wait. A computer the size of a room just stops working?
The team opened it up and found a moth stuck in relay number seventy.
No way! So that is where the word bug comes from?
Not quite. Engineers called glitches bugs long before. Edison did in 1878.
They taped the moth into the logbook: first actual case of bug being found.
And we still call fixing code debugging!
